summary.headline: SMS Pharma FY26 revenue rose 13% to INR887 crores and EBITDA margin reached 20%; FY27 guidance is 15% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR238 crores with EBITDA of INR40 crores (17% margin) and gross margin down about 2% QoQ on higher solvent costs. For FY26, revenue grew 13% to INR887 crores, EBITDA rose 23% to INR171 crores (20% margin), and PAT rose 47% to INR102 crores, including INR14 crores from associate VKT Pharma. Management framed FY26 as a foundation-building year, with benefits expected in FY27 and FY28 from backward integration, new products and capacity. FY27 guidance is 15% revenue growth and an EBITDA margin above 20%, with management citing Middle East logistics risk as the reason for prudence.

segments.name: ARV APIs
segments.commentary: Management says superior cost structure has won market share and customer relationships; recently commercialised products showing encouraging traction. No segment revenue figure was given.

segments.name: Anti-inflammatory APIs (ibuprofen)
segments.commentary: Ibuprofen is roughly 20% of total revenue and the main contributor to this segment; progressive volume growth with a significant part of planned capacity already committed for next year.

segments.name: Anti-diabetic APIs
segments.commentary: Management said it consciously redirected focus from this segment from the beginning of Q3 FY26 because of pricing and demand changes, favouring ARVs and anti-inflammatory APIs.

segments.name: Anti-erectile and anti-ulcer APIs
segments.commentary: Long-standing segments described as stable and among the top three for the company; new products are being launched in these.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15%, with management aiming to improve on the FY26 EBITDA margin of 20%.
Management says growth could exceed guidance if the Middle East situation and logistics stabilise.
Management targets a 22% EBITDA margin next year (FY27), near the company's historical high, and says it aims to exceed that thereafter.
Management's medium-term target is 20-25% growth; it projects lower for conservatism.
Brownfield expansion (about INR280 crores total, about INR130 crores invested so far) is expected to complete by March 2027 and contribute incrementally from FY28, with further scale-up in FY29.
Peptides and CDMO updates are promised after the next two quarters; peptide contribution is expected from FY29.
capex_capacity: Ibuprofen backward-integration capex will raise installed capacity from 500 to 800 metric tons per month on completion in FY27; management says existing capacity is about 80% utilised.
Brownfield block of about INR280 crores total investment, with about INR130 crores spent so far, will house 4-5 new high-margin APIs, which current capacity cannot support.
Capacity utilisation is expected to reach a high level by FY28.
Current capex completion is targeted for March 2027, with incremental revenue from FY28.
Filed 12 DMFs/CEPs in FY26; plans 10 more filings in FY27 and 10 in FY28.
demand_pricing: Solvent costs rose sharply in March 2026 because of the war, which lifted raw material cost and cut gross margin by about 2% QoQ.
Ibuprofen prices are rising because of the war; management credits backward integration for competitiveness and customer confidence.
High-value products were 47% of sales per the analyst; management expects this to rise to about 60% in the medium term with the new APIs.
Exports are about 70% of India business revenue, expected to stay in the 70-75% range.
Five new products are being developed for JV partner Chemo, expected to commercialise in FY27; management compares the potential to past anti-diabetic growth.
One of the largest customers accounts for 28% of FY26 revenue, spread across multiple products (customer not named).

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin fell about 2% QoQ because raw material consumption rose, driven by March solvent price increases caused by the war.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex breakup and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen backward integration takes capacity from 500 to 800 MT per month; a brownfield block of 4-5 new APIs is also being built. Both are due by March 2027, with incremental revenue from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are achievable in the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the company's all-time high is about 22%, that it targets 22% in FY27 from 20% in FY26, and that it aims to exceed that afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin expansion, and which molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited backward integration into intermediates, mainly for ibuprofen, plus the four or five new APIs, which are in new therapeutic categories and not the major ones. Management expects high-value share to rise to about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the related-party transaction exposure with VKT Pharma and SMS Life Sciences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMS sells APIs to VKT (about INR40 crores), which it holds about 34-35% of. SMS Life Sciences is a promoter-linked company (about INR20 crores of procurement), with no investment by SMS Pharma. No plans to consolidate either entity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is ibuprofen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ibuprofen is roughly 20% of total revenue.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict affecting logistics, freight, and raw material and finished goods supply; solvent costs are rising.
Gross margin pressure from raw material inflation in Q1 FY27 if solvent prices stay high.
Brownfield and capex timing (March 2027 completion) and utilisation ramp in FY28.
Customer concentration: one customer is 28% of FY26 revenue.
Ibuprofen concentration: about 20% of revenue, and the 800 MT capacity plan depends on it.
Related-party transactions with VKT Pharma (about INR40 crores) and SMS Life Sciences (about INR20 crores), with no plans to restructure.
Peptide and CDMO commercial updates deferred for two quarters.
Operating cash flow conversion: management says it plans to strengthen this further, with no figure given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and margin drivers, but explicitly prudent on FY27 guidance because of the Middle East conflict. Answers on the anti-diabetic segment, peptides, CDMO and customer names were brief or deferred to later quarters. Some answers were unclear or required corrections during the call.
